Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans

Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.

The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt.

The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".

The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help".

"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said.

Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.

Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side, Moreno said.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.

The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.

On Saturday, Moreno said that nine people are still in hospital.

She said that the captain of the ship was injured in the accident but refused medical treatment until he knew all passengers and crew were accounted for.

US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue had been an "incredible job".

Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued.

Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what had occurred.

Still covered in dirt from the boat crash, Joe Knab of Kansas told New Orleans NBC affiliate WDSU that the ship quickly capsized after the collision.

He spent about 20 minutes in the water before being rescued.

"When we first went in we were bobbing underneath the water; it was sinking pretty fast, but we finally got out of there," he said.

Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he had seen the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision.

"It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic."

Holford added that he had seen passengers and crew "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking.

The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website.

Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

India's Gen Z protesters are facing the limits of dissent

Cheers erupted at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site in July as news broke that Gen-Z protests had forced federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign.

One protester turned to me, beaming: "This is the youth's victory."

Just over three months later, the mood has shifted dramatically. Student protesters are now struggling even to assemble. Demonstrations by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) last month over voting rights were met with sweeping restrictions and thousands of peaceful protesters were detained .

The summer had seen a new wave of dissent in India, driven by deep frustration among the youth and fuelled by irreverent online satire.

The movement spread across the country, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a leader with a strongman image, unaccustomed to open criticism or mockery, struggled to contain it. But the government's increasingly forceful security response suggests it has learned from its rare concession to protesters, invoking public order to curb dissent.

The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national spokesperson Syed Zafar Islam rejected accusations of heavy-handedness and told the BBC: "The right to protest and freedom of expression is mandated by the constitution, but it has to be done within the law. It cannot override the rights of others, at the cost of public security".

This is by no means the first time the Modi government has faced large-scale protests.

But the breadth of them pose a challenge for the BJP, according to Yamini Aiyar, former president of the Centre for Policy Research and visiting professor at Brown University.

The CJP led massive protests in July which ended with the resignation of a federal minister

"They are not defined by caste, gender or economic class," Aiyar said. "Even some of the core BJP base, the upwardly mobile, lower-income classes, were attracted by the movement."

The scale of the youth protests is also magnified by its online presence. Protesters have broken a longstanding political taboo, openly mocking the prime minister online.

"It's more than just laughs," said Sakhi, a student protester who identifies as they/them and affiliated with one of Delhi University's left-wing student organisations.

"The fear of repercussions in other generations isn't felt as much in ours," they said. "Comedy is a new language to challenge authority."

Previous protest movements posed serious challenges to Modi but were easier to dismiss as representing narrow sections of society or to label "anti-national", according to Aiyar.

In 2020, farmers protesting against controversial agricultural reforms were blocked from entering Delhi, leading to months of demonstrations and, at times, clashes on the capital's borders. After a year of protests, the government abandoned the reforms.

Protests against a contentious citizenship law in 2019 and 2020 are a stark reminder of the powers of the judiciary should anyone be deemed a national security threat.

Student activist Umar Khalid was arrested under anti-terror laws after violent clashes in Delhi that killed 53 people, mostly Muslims. He was accused of being a "key conspirator". He has now spent more than six years in jail without his trial having begun.

His partner Banojyotsna Lahiri told the BBC they have no regrets, but that the situation instilled "a kind of fear that has prevailed".

The CJP in its early days became a unifier for Indian youth frustrated with the state of education, jobs and economy

"We are just looking at a very dark mesh of empty space, because we don't know when the endpoint is," Lahiri said. Khalid's latest appeal was lodged this month.

Aiyar believes opponents are using a familiar "playbook" today to "de-legitimise" protests, but that it isn't resonating as convincingly.

Nevertheless, the youth protests have struggled to recapture this summer's momentum.

CJP leaders, including spokesperson Saurav Das, have faced repeated detentions and legal action. Das and fellow leader Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in Delhi's Tihar jail after being accused of trespassing at Jantar Mantar.

The site of their summer victory has since been struck off the list of authorised protest venues, a decision being challenged in court.

Protesters from other groups, including the left-wing All India Students' Association (Aisa), have also faced police action over allegations of defying orders.

"We were expecting some kind of crackdown," said Das. He added that "the government has learnt a lot" since the summer.

Legal experts warn the proceedings themselves can have a chilling effect.

"A lot of cases can lead to acquittals, but it can take years. The process is the punishment, and that can deter protesters," said Ali Khan, an assistant professor at Lloyd Law College.

The restrictions on demonstrations have become excessive, according to constitutional lawyer Vrinda Grover, who is advising the CJP.

Tens of thousands of people gathered at Delhi's iconic Ramlila Maidan for the opposition protest on 1 November

"Those who are organising the protests have repeatedly emphasised that this is non-violent," she argued. "Rights have been whittled down in the name of law and order."

The BJP has rejected suggestions it is suppressing peaceful dissent.

Islam told the BBC that demonstrations "cannot override the rights of other citizens just because a handful of people want to protest and be responsible for violence".

Even dissenting online carries risk. Sakhi's viral social media posts have attracted targeted abuse and transphobic attacks. The BBC has seen posts threatening them with violence and rape.

Sometimes, it can deter Sakhi from protesting or even make them change the way they dress.

"Making people laugh can turn into being called anti-national," Sakhi said. "They want me to feel damaged," they added.

They claim some of their content was removed after getting millions of views.

Under India's information technology laws, the government can order platforms to block content on national security grounds. Notices on X and Instagram have shown accounts being withheld in India.

CJP leaders have likened the crackdown to the 1975 Emergency, when then prime minister Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties and jailed political opponents.

Opposition parties have, in part, filled the void. Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi on 1 November for a rally organised by INDIA bloc , an alliance of opposition parties led by Congress, and permitted by the authorities.

CJP leaders, meanwhile, insist the movement is bigger than their organisation.

When Das walked out Delhi's Tihar prison on 21 October, photographs showed him smiling.

"I would just say wait and watch," Das told us. "Time is on our side. We are a very young generation."

Highlights: France narrowly beat South Africa in thriller in Paris

Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang, Attissogbe, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Lucu (3)

Tries: Wessels, Reinach, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2)

France held on to end their five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France with an enthralling 21-19 victory in Paris.

The victory dents the world champions' hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final and puts Les Bleus in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings.

The hosts, inspired by their captain Antoine Dupont, showed their class and skill to score three tries in a frantic first half.

France's back three of Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossed in a thrilling opening 40 minutes, with Jan-Hendrik Wessels scoring off the back of a maul for the visitors.

The Springboks thought they had a second try on the stroke of half-time but Kurt-Lee Arendse's try was chalked off after he strayed marginally offside.

Number eight Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card early in the second half - the third of five cards shown in an incident-packed game - for a dangerous shoulder charge, but it had the opposite effect to derailing the world champions.

With South Africa's set-piece power proving too much, replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcolm Marx scored to set up a thrilling finale.

However, Manie Libbok missed the vital conversion to Marx's try that would have levelled the game.

With South Africa pushing for a winning score, Bielle-Biarrey produced a huge defensive tackle to force the ball loose, before Dupont, who was named player of the match, gathered possession to help seal the victory.

The result will come as a blow to both England and Ireland, who are in direct competition with France for a place in the Nations Championship final at the end of the month.

Les Bleus, who are six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings, now face Argentina next Saturday, putting them in a strong position to reach the inaugural final at Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 29 November.

Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang celebrated France's first try but the hosts did not score a point in the second half

Injuries to France's three first-choice fly-halves - Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack and Antoine Hastoy - left France coach Fabien Galthie with little option but to deploy his captain and talismanic scrum-half at number 10.

Despite wearing the France number 10 shirt for the first time, Dupont lined up at scrum-half, as Galthie played Rassie Erasmus, who had swapped his entire front row an hour before kick-off, at his own game.

It was an electric start from the hosts, as a clever move sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap, with Grandidier-Nkanang eventually crossing in the corner.

A monstrous left-footed 50:22 from Dupont, with South Africa lock Lood de Jager in the sin-bin for a high tackle, gave France field position, before the ball cannoned off Gourgues' head and Attissogbe crossed for a fortunate try.

Dupont supplied more magic, grubber kicking through on his stronger right foot for Bielle-Biarrey to race over.

South Africa's power told as they scored their opening try from a maul, before Erasmus changed his entire front row again, five minutes before half-time.

Dupont did slot in at fly-half but mainly was deployed in his familiar position of scrum-half

Creativity, intensity and physicality - it was a first game that felt remarkably similar to the epic quarter-final of the 2023 Rugby World Cup in Paris.

Despite losing Wiese to a 20-minute red card early in the second half, the world champions took advantage of Grandidier-Nkanang's sin-bin for a deliberate knock-on.

Tiredness and poor discipline made the game loose and chaotic, before the Springboks turned to their scrum to regain control.

A succession of scrum penalties resulted in another sin-bin, with replacement France prop Regis Montagne yellow carded as the hosts were left clinging on for the final 10 minutes.

Stunning scramble defence and sheer grit showed a side to the back-to-back Six Nations champions France that has often been questioned.

Despite their scrum crumbling, France held firm, continuing to chase kicks and compete for loose balls.

A draw would have felt a fair result given the contrasting nature of the two halves, but Libbok - as at the 2023 World Cup - badly shanked a kick that will once again raise questions over his ability to deliver under pressure in the biggest Test matches.

For once, the fine margins went against South Africa, who won every knockout game of the last World Cup by a point.

They face Ireland in Dublin next Saturday and will now likely need a favour from England, who take on New Zealand earlier that same day, if they are to reclaim top spot in the southern hemisphere standings.

A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.

On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips.

For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets.

With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years.

Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns.

But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere.

Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips.

It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.

Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.

The city-state has had some success in policing this.

It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places.

They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties.

In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore.

The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere.

Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed.

But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department.

Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud.

In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months.

Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case.

Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing.

In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times.

Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses.

Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity.

On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government".

China has also long rebuffed accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips.

Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following a board meeting

How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness.

In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively.

For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law.

But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities.

Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case.

BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road.

In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed.

Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man.

During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS.

Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences.

Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government.

Alice Huang, seen here in Taipei with Jensen Huang last year, ran Megaspeed for several months in 2023

All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore.

"For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said.

Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore".

But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips.

With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts.

Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.

Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said.

"Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said.

But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China".

"This is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour."

Additional reporting by Jack Lau of the BBC's Global China Unit.

Maggie Heginbothom was married in her hospital room at Ysbyty Gwynedd

A woman with a terminal cancer diagnosis married her partner of 15 years in the hospital where she is receiving palliative care - and her horses even made the ceremony.

Maggie Heginbothom, 68, who has advanced liver cancer, thanked staff at Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor for organising a wedding ceremony on Monday, just two days after her partner Mark proposed.

The horse lover and former clinical scientist with Public Health Wales, described hospital staff as being "like family to me".

"It was so beautiful and I honestly never thought it was going to be possible, especially seeing both my horses there as well," she said.

Heginbothom, originally from the Vale of Glamorgan, was admitted to hospital nearly three weeks ago after becoming unwell while riding one of her horses.

After her partner proposed from her hospital bedside, staff on the Tegid Ward volunteered to pull together a celebration that included flowers, decorations, a harpist, food, cake and Heginbothom's beloved horses Ozzy and Quiosque.

Horse lover Heginbothom says the "little touches" made her wedding special

The horses were brought to the hospital by Pen Llŷn Stud and Riding School, where Heginbothom rode and competed for many years.

"From the beautiful decorations to all the little touches that made our wedding so special, I cannot thank them enough," she said.

Ward manager Rachel Parry said her team were determined to get things right.

"On the morning of the wedding, we transformed Maggie's room with white sheets and fairy lights to create a beautiful space for the ceremony, while the relatives' room became a reception area," she said.

Staff at the hospital joined the "special and emotional" celebrations

"Everything ran like clockwork, and some of our colleagues even came in on their days off to help make it happen.

"It was such a special and emotional occasion.

"There wasn't a dry eye in the room, and it was particularly lovely that some of the other patients Maggie has got to know during her time on the ward were able to join the celebrations."

Matron Ceri Newell said it was an example of the compassion and dedication shown by NHS staff.

"Nursing is about so much more than treating illness," she said.

"It is about compassion, kindness, humanity and recognising that sometimes the most important thing we can do is help make someone's wishes come true.

"What the team achieved for Maggie and Mark in such a short space of time was truly remarkable, and I could not be prouder of every single person involved.

"Everyone went above and beyond, working together to create something incredibly special for a couple going through such a difficult time.

"Moments like these remind us why we do what we do, and I am so proud of what the team achieved."

Duncan Ferguson's home debut with Glentoran ended with a late winner from teenage striker Cal Weatherup

At the third time of asking, Duncan Ferguson is finally up and running as Glentoran manager.

After two draws to start his tenure in the Irish Premiership, a home debut for the former Everton striker had late drama under the Friday night lights at the Oval.

Jordan Stewart, dubbed the "wee man" by big Dunc after his first game, celebrated his contract extension by scoring the opening goal and, in a largely uneventful game, it looked like that would be the difference.

However, that all changed when Ben Cushnie equalised for Bangor in the 83rd minute, but there was more drama to follow as Cal Weatherup raced onto a long ball to slot home the winner with three minutes remaining and secure a first win for Ferguson as boss.

"I'm delighted to get my first three points at home, I'm absolutely made up," Ferguson said after the game.

"The boys kept on going until the very end."

Weatherup's late goal gives Ferguson first Glens win

All the goals and reports from the Irish Premiership

Ferguson's first game in the Irish League was meant to be at home to Ballymena United on 24 October, but Storm Boelo and a waterlogged pitch delayed his highly-anticipated debut in the league.

Stewart scored the equaliser at then-leaders Coleraine in his first outing in the dugout the following week, and the Glens were then held to a goalless draw at Carrick Rangers.

But on Friday, Ferguson finally announced himself to the home support in east Belfast.

Despite a controlled first half and Stewart's opener, Ferguson felt that his side "sat too deep" before Bangor's equaliser, which came through former Glentoran man Cushnie.

But it was teenager Weatherup who was ultimately the difference, with a finish that Ferguson would have been proud of in his playing days as he slotted the ball between the legs of the onrushing Patrick Solis Grogan for his first goal of the campaign.

Ferguson said he was "made up" for the 18-year-old, who replaced Pat Hoban midway through the second half.

"We showed good character. We showed a bit of resilience," added the 54-year-old.

"They put us under pressure in the second half but that will happen. You're not going to dominate a game for the whole game at any level.

"I was delighted the boys showed character and resilience to get back into the game."

Highlights: Late winner gives Ferguson first victory as Glens boss

Given their mixed start to the season, a charge at the Irish Premiership title is going to be a long shot.

But if the Glens are to have any aspirations of a first Gibson Cup since 2009 then it is important for them to keep pace with those above.

Leaders Linfield and nearest challengers Coleraine both were comfortable winners on Friday, while Larne bounced back from their poor recent win to beat Dungannon Swifts.

Glentoran are 14 points off the Blues but have a game in hand, and they face another tricky home test against Cliftonville next Friday to try and build upon the win over the Seasiders.

As he reflected on his start to the league, Ferguson admitted "I think we need to get better overall.

"We're not conceding many goals, but we just have to create more.

"That's the hardest part of the game, but we look solid and that's the main thing.

"I'm happy with the group and the league is very close together, from top to bottom".

With that in mind, especially as he continues his early steps in the league, it's just "one game at a time" for Ferguson, rather than thinking too far ahead.

"We've just got to keep going. I think that is seven or eight games undefeated now," he added.

"We have to keep going and keep winning. We're a big club and the fans want us to keep winning, and I'm glad we got the three points for them today."

Toby Alderweireld was part of the Tottenham team that reached the Champions League final under Mauricio Pochettino

Mauricio Pochettino heads to Old Trafford with a reputation for "brutal" pre-seasons, an obsession with fitness and a no-nonsense approach.

Manchester United confirmed on Friday that Pochettino will become their manager on 18 November - replacing Michael Carrick - and has signed a contract until June 2029.

So what should the players and staff expect when the Argentine takes control at the end of next week?

BBC Sport spoke to Toby Alderweireld, who spent four years playing for Pochettino at Tottenham during a successful period where they reached the Champions League final and finished second in the Premier League.

How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd

Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better

Alderweireld, 37, says Pochettino has a no-nonsense approach to management and that he can get the best out of a squad, as long as you do it his way.

"He is very approachable but you need to follow his plan. If you don't follow his plan, you go on the side and you're not coming back any more.

"You need to think about team, team, team. If you're thinking about yourself, you're gone.

"As a player you have your own life, your own situation but he says 'look, I understand and you can talk to me about it but the team is number one' - that's the way it is and if you're not following it, he'll put you on the sideline.

"He's straightforward, has his own ideas and maybe you agree with them or don't, that's up to you. But you need to follow him and I think that's something Manchester United need - a big character, everyone in the same direction, following the plan and if not, no problem, you can go. He's the main man.

"He's a very smart man, knows how to talk to the press and what to say. He will create an environment like 'it's us against the world' - we are getting fit, we are together as a team. It doesn't matter what people say, let's work together and get results together.

"At Spurs there was coaching staff but he will be there. He knows everything. If he's not there, he's looking at video and data. He knows everything about the players on and off the pitch - the players will be watched.

"He is, in a positive way, a control freak because he says your body is your weapon and it needs to be ready to perform."

Does Alderweireld think Pochettino is right for Man Utd?

Manchester United have been criticised this season for an apparent lack of fitness and for not running enough in games - they rank in the bottom five in the league for distance covered and most high-intensity runs.

Alderweireld says Pochettino's number one demand is fitness and running .

"First of all he made us very fit. Pre-season was brutal.

"The way he wants to play - on the front foot, putting people under pressure, a high line, very dynamic play - you need to run. You need to be capable of running and be capable of high intensity runs - the basic is to be fit.

"Every manager wants a good pre-season and time to give the players their ideas and the fitness. But the players are going to feel straight away that it's a different level.

"This is every day at the training ground, it's 100% - that's what he asks, what he demands. It will be a big difference for the players and they're going to see results there straight away.

"In the Champions League semi-final, we were 3-0 down [against Ajax] and he didn't have a tactical half-time talk. He just said 'you're going to be physical, you're going to fight, you only need one goal to be back in the game, believe that everything is possible'.

"That was a big moment because we were nowhere near Ajax at that time, especially in that game. But we changed everything by intensity, by duels. I remember the long ball to [Fernando] Llorente and just fighting and asking 'how badly do you want it?' It changed from that moment."

Jesus Owono plays for Equatorial Guinea at international level

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee after his challenge which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during the closing stages of the second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November.

De Miguel died the following day, aged 30.

The disciplinary committee said it had to base its decision "on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report", which stated the player "was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'.

"The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge."

The committee added the "nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances" means that "the maximum sanction, a 12-match suspension, is justified".

Separately, the federation has decided the game between the two sides, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred, will not be replayed.

"This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred," it said.

The teams were drawing 2-2 at the time and that result will now stand, with a federation committee saying that was the "most respectful course of action, given the extraordinary and tragic circumstances of this case".

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on 4 November, in which he said he was experiencing "the most difficult days" of his life and felt "enormous pain" about De Miguel's death.

On Thursday, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said Equatorial Guinea international Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the incident.

Manso said Owono is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return, adding: "What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.

"We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

"When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so]."

BAMAKO – Rwanda’s hopes of maintaining their perfect start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying campaign suffered a setback on Friday, November 13, after Amavubi twice took the lead against Mali but eventually lost 3-2 in Bamako.

In a contested game that offered Rwanda a genuine opportunity to claim a significant result away from home, the visitors demonstrated attacking intent and resilience, scoring twice against one of Africa’s formidable football sides.

However, their inability to protect those advantages proved costly as Mali fought back to secure all three points.

The result was particularly disappointing for Rwanda because they had shown, for much of the encounter, that they could trouble their highly rated hosts.

Jojea Kwizera gave Amavubi the lead in the 28th minute, rewarding Rwanda’s efforts with a goal that briefly put them in control of the contest.

Mali, however, responded before the interval, restoring parity in the 42nd minute to ensure the teams went into the dressing rooms level at 1-1.

Rwanda returned from the break with renewed determination and needed only eight minutes to reclaim the advantage.

A carefully worked corner routine, beginning with a short delivery, created the opportunity for Phanuel Kavita to rise above the Mali defenders and direct a powerful header into the net in the 53rd minute.

It was an important moment for Amavubi, who had managed to respond to Mali’s equalizer rather than allow the home side to dictate the second-half proceedings.

The lead, however, proved difficult to defend as Mali increased their attacking pressure.

The hosts had already threatened twice in quick succession, with Mahamadou Doumbia striking the right post in the 52nd minute before Moussa Kounfolo Yeo rattled the woodwork again five minutes later with a long-range effort.

Rwanda’s defenders managed to clear the danger on the latter occasion, but Mali continued to search for openings.

Their persistence paid off in the 63rd minute when Yeo found the equalizer, bringing the score to 2-2 and shifting the momentum back towards the hosts.

Mali subsequently introduced fresh attacking options, with Gaoussou Diakite and Mohamadou Kante among those brought on as the home side sought a decisive breakthrough.

Kwizera tested the Mali goalkeeper in the 60th minute, while Mickels Joy Lance came particularly close in the 81st minute after a promising counter-attacking move that briefly left three Rwandan players against one Mali defender.

However, the goalkeeper stood firm to deny the visitors what could have been a crucial third goal.

With the match approaching its final stages, Mali eventually found the breakthrough that Rwanda had worked hard to prevent.

Mohamadou Kante rose to head home from a corner in the 85th minute, completing the hosts’ comeback and leaving Amavubi with little time to rescue a point.

Four minutes of added time offered no further goals, confirming a painful defeat for the Rwandan side.

A Difficult Test, But Another Opportunity Awaits

Before the encounter, Rwanda captain Djihad Bizimana had acknowledged Mali’s strength, describing them as one of Africa’s top football sides while insisting that Amavubi had earned their position in the qualifying group and would be difficult opponents.

Rwanda demonstrated much of that determination in Bamako, particularly through their ability to score twice and repeatedly threaten the hosts.

However, the result also exposed the importance of defensive concentration, especially when playing away against opponents capable of sustaining pressure and punishing mistakes.

Despite the disappointment, Rwanda will not have to wait long for an opportunity to respond. The two sides are scheduled to meet again on November 17, this time in Kigali, where Amavubi will have the backing of their home supporters.

The return fixture offers Rwanda an immediate chance to address the shortcomings exposed in Bamako and demonstrate that the two-goal attacking performance was not an isolated achievement.

For a team that had travelled to Mali believing it could compete, the defeat will hurt. But the manner in which Amavubi twice took the lead provides a foundation from which they can approach the next encounter with renewed belief.

Following the defeat, Mali move to the top of Group K with nine points from three matches, while Rwanda drop to second with six points. Cape Verde occupy third place on three points after beating Liberia 4-2, leaving Liberia bottom without a point.

The group’s fourth round of matches is scheduled for Tuesday, November 17, when Rwanda host Mali in Kigali, while Liberia welcome Cape Verde. The two encounters will be important in determining how the group shapes up heading into the final two rounds of qualifying.

Products such as Microsoft Teams and Outlook have been out of service for much of Friday

Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.

The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.

The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.

Microsoft apologised for the technical issue, which it said was introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and was not caused by a cyber-attack or an artificial intelligence agent.

Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers.

Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday.

By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America.

Services were beginning to recover by Friday afternoon UK time, nearly 24 hours after the issues first began to emerge.

Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?

Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

In the UK, some parts of the NHS were affected , as were some schools and police forces.

UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls and that there had been no disruption to the transport network.

In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails.

In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook.

Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday.

In Turkey, advisers and officials attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya were left frustrated by being unable to access Outlook.

The issues also affected smaller businesses and individuals.

Pete says his business has been brought to a standstill

Peter Pentz, a winemaker in South Africa, said his entire business had been effectively brought to a "standstill".

His winery's communication with exports was also brought to a standstill, he said, and "critical production work" had been halted as the Cape West Coast winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day operations".

Georgia from Staffordshire in England said she had been due to complete her first house purchase after waiting eight months to get to this point - but the outage has delayed that.

"The solicitor mentioned there may be a delay due to not being able to contact other agencies," she said.

"We're not the only one completing today - there are hundreds of houses and for them to ring everyone in time is unfeasible."

Microsoft first acknowledged users in the Americas were unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday, and shortly after warned the disruption was possibly affecting Microsoft 365 globally.

It launched an investigation and engineers began working to restore services, but by 04:36 on Friday Microsoft was reporting only a "partial recovery" in some parts of the world.

By 13:32, the tech giant said there had been "broader improvements" in North America, "sustained improvements" across much of Europe and "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia Pacific region.

Microsoft said it restored services gradually due to the scale of the problem and to help ensure services remained stable once they were up and running again.

"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," a Microsoft spokesperson said.

"We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously."

A full post-incident report will be released once Microsoft has completed a review.

Experts said that while workers may have been happy to not have email access for a working day, the incident showed the dependence many organisations have on these cloud-based services.

"The global Microsoft outage is a stark reminder of how heavily we rely on a handful of big tech providers," said Rob Demain, chief executive of cybersecurity firm e2e-assure.

Matt Saunders, field chief technology officer at tech consultancy Adaptavist, said it would be challenging to mitigate against a similar problem.

"Classic IT disaster planning strategies suggest using a second service for resilience, but in practice, it's almost impossible for a business to function without tools such as Microsoft," he said .

"In the wake of this outage, organisations must have a plan in place for how to work without such tools, for when incidents like this occur."

'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth

SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket for the first time, after a flight lasting 22-and-a-half hours.

The rocket returned to Earth and hovered near its launch tower, whose mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - then secured it.

The company had hoped to catch the bottom part of the rocket as well, but this was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday.

SpaceX needs to reliably recover both parts of Starship so that it can fly repeatedly and drastically reduce costs.

The moment the rocket came back to Earth

The Starship rocket launched successfully on Friday

There were loud cheers from SpaceX staff who were watching the flight as the rocket returned to the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas.

This is the 15th test of Starship and the first that hoped to fully recover both parts of the rocket. SpaceX wants to make the top and bottom sections of Starship fully reusable.

The 124m-tall (407ft) rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:47 local time (19:47 GMT) on Friday.

The plan was to grab the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six-and-a-half-minutes later when it returned.

But the booster activated an automated abort, diverting instead to the ocean where it hovered above the water before exploding.

Elon Musk later posted on X that the booster had been "slightly low on fuel".

The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean and burst into flames

The top part of the rocket continued its journey to space where it deployed 26 satellites, which form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet.

The Ship completed 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower.

SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights.

But this was the first time the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has been grabbed by the "chopsticks".

Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it was in space.

Any problems would have resulted in the ship being brought down in the ocean in the same way as the booster.

A SpaceX lander could take astronauts down to the surface of the Moon

Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX.

In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster.

Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than 100 times a year and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch.

Landing an entire Starship rocket would take spaceflight to the next level, said Prof Malcolm Macdonald, president of Royal Aeronautical Society - but it didn't happen this time.

"Not recovering the first stage is a setback. But they have recovered Super Heavy before and so successfully returning and recovering the Ship is a substantial step forward," he added.

"They have demonstrated the two halves of the recovery challenge, just not yet on the same flight.

"The next milestone would be stitching those achievements together and then proving they can do it reliably, repeatedly and economically."

After SpaceX became a public company earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will Nasa.

The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline.

What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next?

Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test

SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface.

But it is not the only company working with Nasa. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touchdown.

Both companies will also play a key role in the Artemis III mission, which is currently planned for summer 2027 - another challenging schedule.

Four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft will attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers during the voyage.

Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended.

But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida.

Blue Origin had said its spacecraft would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027.

Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said the US was in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy took over as head coach in July 2024

As the first snow of the season falls in Oslo, the clean-up operation at Norway's home stadium is in full swing – tractors on the pitch, Norwegian Football Federation staff getting stuck in with their shovels.

This has been a problematic pitch in the past, with even the great Erling Haaland questioning its condition , external back in March, before it was fixed during the summer.

By their recent, historic high standards, Norway need something of a repair job themselves.

Having gone through 2025 unbeaten and then soared to the quarter-finals of the World Cup, Norway have lost three games in a row for the first time in a decade.

Granted, two of those were against Portugal, whereas their losing run in 2016 included defeats in Azerbaijan and Belarus.

But this is Norway's golden generation. With Haaland, Martin Odegaard and a glut of other elite talents at their disposal, expectations are greater than ever.

Thumping Italy twice on their way to World Cup qualification was one thing – their first major tournament since 1998 – but beating Brazil in their last-16 tie in New Jersey underlined their credentials as an emerging force in international football.

So, when this Nations League campaign came around, Stale Solbakken's men were expected to be jostling with Portugal for top spot.

Instead, they find themselves at the bottom of Group A4 with just one win from four games, level with third-placed Wales on three points but below them because of their head-to-head record.

How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done

Odegaard backing Norway to avenge Wales defeat

Wales' only victory of the campaign so far was against Norway in Cardiff a month ago, and on Saturday they are bidding to join Portugal and world champions Spain as the only teams to win competitive matches in Oslo over the past three years.

"The way we look at it is this is the type of game we want to be playing in," Wales head coach Craig Bellamy tells BBC Sport Wales.

"I see a collective team that you have to like but, individually, very much so as well. So that's a good challenge.

"We've all been aware of their threat. The World Cup proved that. And I just don't see them going anywhere for the next five, 10 years either."

There is much on the line for Wales and Norway in Oslo.

While either team could still reach the Nations League quarter-finals, the priority is to avoid relegation from the top tier.

Finishing third or higher would also guarantee top seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying, enabling them to avoid being drawn alongside the continent's heavyweights.

"It'll go a long way to us having an opportunity of being seeded one, which is huge for us, but it isn't going to be given to us," Bellamy adds.

"We have to go out there tomorrow and try and take it. So, for me, it's fight fire with fire. I'm expecting them to really come with big intensity and it's up to us to match it.

Staff clear snow off the pitch at Ullevaal Stadion in Oslo on Friday

If Norway are at the peak of their golden era, Wales are still basking in the afterglow of theirs.

They had been absent from major tournaments for 58 years before a team featuring Gareth Bale and Aaron Ramsey took them to the semi-finals of Euro 2016.

Like Norway's exploits this summer, that tournament in France changed the landscape of Welsh football, paving the way for future qualifications at Euro 2020 and the 2022 World Cup.

"I think that we are both small countries, so I can agree on that," Norway head coach Solbakken says of the comparison.

"Everyone will remember that summer of 2026 in Norway, as Wales did 10 years ago."

What's at stake for Wales against Norway and Portugal?

If you want to stretch the analogy to tenuous lengths, you could also note that the two teams were built around the heroics of hitherto ponytailed forwards (Bale and Haaland) and the creativity of Arsenal playmakers (Ramsey and Odegaard).

Few remain of that Welsh vintage by now, though captain Ben Davies is one.

"They've got players now performing at the highest level in world football and starring in that as well," the Tottenham Hotspur defender says.

"Great for Norwegian football, a challenge for us, but one we're looking forward to."

Davies played an important role in Wales' win over Norway last month, at the heart of a defence which managed to contain Haaland.

The 33-year-old has also been part of a Spurs backline which denied the Norwegian a goal in a 4-0 win at Manchester City two years ago.

Not that Davies is going to mention that in Oslo.

"He's a world-class player," he says. "Maybe he had an off-night [in Cardiff] but we worked hard, stuck to our job and we defended really well. Hopefully we'll do that again."

Mu kiganiro yagiranye n'itangazamakuru, uyu mukandida yavuze ko atumva impamvu hari bamwe bagaragaza impungenge cyangwa bakarwanya igitekerezo cyo gukoresha amatora muri OIF, kandi ari uburyo busanzwe bukoreshwa mu zindi nzego mpuzamahanga zirimo Umuryango w'Abibumbye, UNESCO n'Umuryango wa Afurika Yunze Ubumwe.

Yavuze ko OIF ifite n'inshingano zo gukurikirana amatora, bityo ko bidakwiye ko igira ubwoba bwo gukoresha ubu buryo mu guhitamo abayobozi bayo.

Ati: “Sinzi impamvu twegereye igikorwa cy'itora dufite ubwoba runaka, kandi nyamara amatora asanzwe aba mu bihugu byacu byose. OIF ifite n'inshingano zo gukurikirana amatora, kuko ari inzira ya demokarasi.”

Yasobanuye ko amategeko n'amabwiriza agenga OIF ateganya ko ibihugu bishobora kubanza kugerageza kumvikana ku mukandida umwe, ariko igihe ibyo bitashobotse hakitabazwa amatora.

Ati: “Birumvikana ko ibihugu biramutse byumvikanye ku mukandida, byaba ari byiza. Ariko amategeko yacu ateganya ko mu gihe bitumvikanyweho, hakorwa amatora.”

Uyu mukandida yanenze imyumvire yo kubona amatora nk'ikintu kidakwiye muri OIF, avuga ko bidakwiye ko umuryango wubakiye ku mahame ya demokarasi utinya uburyo bwo gutora.

Ati: “Sinumva impamvu twakagombye gutinya amatora muri OIF, kandi nyamara dutora mu Muryango w'Abibumbye, muri UNESCO no mu Muryango wa Afurika Yunze Ubumwe. Sinumva iyi myitwarire yo kurwanya demokarasi bamwe bagaragaza ku bijyanye n'umuryango ukomeye nka OIF.”

Ku bijyanye n'amahirwe ye muri aya matora, yavuze ko akomeje kwitonda kuko nta mukandida ushobora kwizeza intsinzi mbere y'uko amatora arangira, nubwo we yumva afite ubushobozi bwo guhatanira uwo mwanya.

Ati: “Iyo bigeze ku matora, nta kintu kiba cyarangiye mbere y'uko agera ku musozo. Ndabigendamo ubwitonzi, ariko nanone nzi ko ndi umukandida mwiza.”

Igihugu cya Cambodia kiri mu bihugu Isi yahanze amaso muri uku kwezi k'Ugushyingo 2026, nyuma yo kwakira inama ya 20 y'Umuryango Mpuzamahanga w'Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa (OIF), ihuza abakuru b'ibihugu na za Guverinoma, abahagarariye imiryango mpuzamahanga n'abandi bafatanyabikorwa.

Izagira umwihariko kuko izaberamo amatora y’Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF uzayobora uyu muryango mu gihe cya 2027–2030, aho ishobora gusiga Louise Mushikiwabo yongeye gutorerwa kuyobora uyu muryango muri Manda ya gatatu.

Iyi nama ibera i Phnom Penh, umurwa mukuru wa Cambodia, kuva tariki ya 14 kugeza ku ya 16 Ugushyingo 2026. Ifite insanganyamatsiko igira iti: "Kongera ishoramari mu mahoro hagamijwe iterambere risangiwe n'umutekano urambye."

Kuba ibihugu byinshi byahisemo kwitabira iyi nama ntibishingiye ku rurimi rw'Igifaransa gusa, ahubwo ni uko Francophonie imaze kuba urubuga rukomeye rwa dipolomasi, ubukungu, umuco n'imibanire mpuzamahanga.

Ni Umuryango Mpuzamahanga w'Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa washinzwe ku wa 20 Werurwe 1970 i Niamey muri Niger, ugamije guteza imbere ururimi rw'Igifaransa n'ubufatanye hagati y'ibihugu bifitanye amateka n'umuco bihuriyeho.

Kugeza ubu, ugizwe n'ibihugu na za Guverinoma 90, birimo abanyamuryango buzuye, abafatanyabikorwa n'indorerezi.

Uyu muryango ntuhuriza hamwe gusa ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa nk'ururimi rwa buri munsi, ahubwo unakira ibihugu bifite amateka n'ubufatanye n'uyu muryango, nubwo Igifaransa atari rwo rurimi rukoreshwa cyane muri byo.

Intego zawo zirimo guteza imbere amahoro, demokarasi, uburezi, uburenganzira bwa muntu, ubudasa bw'umuco n'ubufatanye mu bukungu.

Cambodia ni Igihugu cyo mu majyepfo y'uburasirazuba bwa Aziya gifitanye amateka n'Abafaransa, kuko cyahoze mu bihugu byakolonijwe n'u Bufaransa. Cyinjiye muri Francophonie nk'indorerezi mu 1991, gihabwa ubunyamuryango busesuye mu 1993.

Kwakira iyi nama ku nshuro ya mbere ni intambwe ikomeye kuri Cambodia, kuko biyifasha kongera kumenyekana ku rwego mpuzamahanga, kwagura umubano wa dipolomasi no gukurura amahirwe y'ishoramari.

Ni uburyo kandi bwo kugaragaza ko Francophonie itagarukira ku Burayi na Afurika gusa, ahubwo ko ifite n'uruhare muri Aziya.

AMAHORO N'UMUTEKANO KU ISONGA RY'IBIGANIRO

Iyi nama ibaye mu gihe Isi ikomeje guhura n'intambara, amakimbirane ya politiki, umutekano muke n'ihungabana ry'ubukungu.

Abayobozi bazahurira i Phnom Penh bazasuzuma uburyo ibihugu byakongera ubufatanye mu gukumira amakimbirane, guteza imbere ibiganiro bya dipolomasi no kubaka amahoro arambye.

Ibi bifite igisobanuro cyihariye kuri Cambodia na yo yanyuze mu mateka y'intambara mbere yo kongera kwiyubaka.

Abazitabira nama kandi barateganya gushyiraho imyanzuro igaragaza uko Francophonie izakomeza kugira uruhare mu gukemura ibibazo byugarije isi.

LOUISE MUSHIKIWABO N'UBUYOBOZI BWA FRANCOPHONIE

Indi mpamvu iyi nama ikurikiranwa cyane ni uruhare rw'Umunyarwandakazi Louise Mushikiwabo, Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa Francophonie kuva mu 2019.

Uyu mwanya ni wo rwego rwo hejuru mu buyobozi bwa OIF, aho ahagararira umuryango mu rwego mpuzamahanga no guhuza ibikorwa by'ibihugu biwugize.

Iyi nama ibaye mu gihe cy'ingenzi ku miyoborere y'uyu muryango, bityo ibiganiro n'ibyemezo bizafatirwamo bikaba bifite akamaro mu cyerekezo cyawo mu myaka iri imbere.

Uyu Munyarwandakazi Louise Mushikiwabo, usanzwe ari Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF, ari mu bakandida bahatanira kongera kuyobora uyu muryango muri Manda ye ya gatatu nyuma yo kongera gutangwaho umukandida n'u Rwanda.

Azaba ahanganye na Juliana Amato Lumumba wo muri Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, Dr. Coumba Ba wo muri Mauritanie na Dacian Cioloș wo muri Roumanie.

Aya matora ateganyijwe ku wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026, aho abakuru b’ibihugu na za guverinoma 53 bigize OIF bazatora uzayobora uyu muryango mu myaka ine iri imbere.

Ni amatora yajemo rwaserera nyuma y'uko Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo iri mu bikorwa byo gushaka kubuza Louise Mushikiwabo kongera gutorerwa kuwuyobora, birimo gusaba ko hahindurwa uburyo amajwi azabarwa.

Jeune Afrique iherutse gutangaza ko hari amakuru amaze igihe avugwa ko Perezida Félix Tshisekedi wa DRC ashobora gukura igihugu cye muri OIF mu gihe Mushikiwabo yakongera gutorwa. Ntihavuzwe niba Tshisekedi yarigeze yemeza cyangwa ngo ahakane ayo makuru.

Icyakora, RDC iramutse ivuyemo, byagira uburemere kuri OIF. RDC ifite abantu miliyoni 67,8 bavuga Igifaransa, ikaba ari cyo gihugu gifite benshi ku Isi, imbere y’u Bufaransa.

Nubwo bimeze gutyo ariko Mushikiwabo avuga ko umuyobozi wa OIF akwiye gutorwa hashingiwe ku bushobozi bwe no ku cyo ashobora kugeza ku muryango, aho kumushingira ku makimbirane igihugu akomokamo gifitanye n’ibindi.

Mu kiganiro yagiranye na Africa 24, Louise Mushikiwabo yavuze ko atumva impamvu amatora y'umwanya w'Ubunyamabanga bw'uyu muryango ateye abantu ubwoba kandi ategurwa akaba mu bwisanzure na Demukarasi.

Yavuze kandi ko abantu badakwiye kuyagirira ubwoba nyamara basanzwe bitabira amatora arimo ay'Umuryango w'Abibumbye, muri UNESCO ndetse no mu muryango wa Afurika Yunze Ubumwe.

Mushikiwabo yatowe bwa mbere mu 2018, atangira inshingano muri Mutarama 2019, yongera gutorwa mu 2022.

Mu byo yakoze ku buyobozi bwe harimo kugabanya no gukomatanya imishinga ya OIF, ikava kuri 40 ikagera kuri 15, kugira ngo ubushobozi bw’umuryango bwibande ku bikorwa bifite umusaruro ugaragara.

Kuva mu 2019, OIF yakusanyije miliyoni 336 z’amayero. Ikigega La Francophonie avec Elles, cyatangijwe mu gihe cya COVID-19, cyageze ku bagore hafi ibihumbi 100, binyuze mu mishinga 354 yo mu bihugu 36.

Mu byo ateganya gukora aramutse yongeye kugirirwa icyizere, harimo ko ashaka kwagura amahugurwa y’urubyiruko mu ikoranabuhanga n’imyuga, akagera ku bihumbi 100 mu cyiciro cya mbere, no guharanira ko indimi n’umuco bya Afurika bigira umwanya mu iterambere ry’ubwenge buhangano.

U Rwanda rufite umwanya wihariye muri iyi nama kubera uruhare rufite muri Francophonie ndetse no kuba Umunyarwandakazi Louise Mushikiwabo ari Umunyamabanga Mukuru wayo.

Perezida Paul Kagame na Madamu Jeannette Kagame kuva tariki 12 Ugushyingo 2026 bari muri Cambodia mu ruzinduko rw'akazi kandi ruri no mu bikorwa bijyanye n'inama ya Francophonie.

Kuri uyu wa Gatanu Perezida Kagame na Madamu Jeannette Kagame bakiriwe mu birori byo kubaha ikaze ku rwego rw’Igihugu n’Umwami wa Cambodia, Preah Bat Samdech Preah Boromneath Norodom Sihamoni, mu ngoro y’Umwami iri mu murwa mukuru Phnom Penh.

Nyuma y’ibirori byo kubakira, Perezida Kagame na Madamu Jeannette Kagame bagiranye ibiganiro byihariye n’Umwami Norodom Sihamoni mu rwego rwo gutangiza uruzinduko rw’akazi Perezida Kagame ari kugirira muri iki gihugu.

Perezida Paul Kagame na Madamu Jeannette Kagame, basuye kandi inzibutso ebyiri z’amateka mu murwa mukuru wa Cambodia, Phnom Penh, mu ruzinduko rw’akazi agirira muri iki gihugu.

Izo nzibutso ni urwibutso rw’Ubwigenge (Independence Monument) ndetse n’urwubatswe mu rwego rwo guha icyubahiro Umwami Norodom Sihanouk wari uzwi nka ‘King-Father’ wa Cambodia, witabye Imana.

Norodom Sihanouk, wahawe izina ry’icyubahiro rya “Preah Borom Ratanak Kaudh”, ni umwe mu bayobozi bagize uruhare rukomeye mu mateka ya Cambodia, by’umwihariko mu rugamba rwo kubona ubwigenge bw’iki gihugu ku butegetsi bw’abakoloni b’Abafaransa mu 1953.

Muri uru ruzinduko Perezida Kagame yagiranye ibiganiro na Minisitiri w'Intebe wa Cambodia, Samdech Hun Manet. Ibihugu byombi kandi byasinyanye amasezerano atatu y'ubufatanye mu ishoramari, ubukerarugendo n'ubwikorezi bwo mu kirere.

Aya masezerano ashobora gufungura amahirwe mashya y'ubucuruzi, koroshya ubufatanye bw'abashoramari no guteza imbere ubukerarugendo hagati y'ibihugu byombi.

U Rwanda kandi rwitabiriye ifungurwa ry'Umudugudu wa Francophonie (Village de la Francophonie), aho rugaragaza umuco warwo n'umurage ndangamuco, rukamenyekanisha ibyo igihugu gifite ku rwego mpuzamahanga.

Mu gihe cy’inkongi buri munota uba ufite agaciro gakomeye mu kurokora ubuzima bw’abari mu nyubako yafashwe. Icyakora, ku bantu bafite ubumuga, ikibazo ntikiba gusa kuba umuriro ushobora kubageraho, ahubwo gishobora no guterwa no kuba hatarateguwe uburyo bashobora kuyisohokamo batagombye gutegereza ko babona ubutabazi bwihariye.

Umuntu ugendera mu igare ry’abafite ubumuga cyangwa undi ufite ubumuga bw’ingingo ashobora kugorwa no gukoresha ingazi mu gihe inyubako yafashwe n’inkongi ifite amagorofa menshi. Utabona na we ashobora kutamenya aho asohokera igihe nta bimenyetso byumvikana cyangwa ubundi buryo bwo kumuyobora buhari, mu gihe ufite ubumuga bwo kutumva ashobora kutamenya ko hatanzwe ubutumwa bumumenyesha ko agomba guhita asohoka.

Mu gihe inkongi z’umuriro zimaze iminsi zibasira inyubako zitandukanye mu Rwanda, abafite ubumuga bagaragaza ko bashobora guhura n’ibibazo bikomeye mu gihe habaye icyo kiza kubera kubura inzira zibafasha gusohoka vuba mu nyubako.

Bagaragaza ko ikibazo cy'imyubakire itita ku bafite ubumuga kitagarukira gusa ku kutabona serivisi zimwe na zimwe, ahubwo kinaba ikibazo cy'umutekano n'uburenganzira bwo gutabarwa no kurokorwa mu gihe habaye impanuka cyangwa ikindi cyago.

Ku wa 10 Ukwakira 2026, inkongi yibasiye inyubako ya GOICO Plaza, isoko rikomeye riri mu Mujyi wa Musanze, yangiza ibintu byinshi by’abaricururizagamo.

Ni inkongi yafashe igice cyo hejuru cy’inyubako y’amagorofa atanu, ikwira mu magorofa yo hasi, ku buryo ahagana saa kumi n’ebyiri z’umugoroba yari yamaze kugera mu bice byose by’inyubako. Imirimo yo kuyizimya yakozwe kugeza mu gitondo cyo ku munsi wakurikiyeho.

Minisiteri y’Ubutegetsi bw’Igihugu yatangaje ko nta muntu wahasize ubuzima, ariko abantu babiri bakomeretse byoroheje, abandi 15 bahabwa ubufasha kubera ihungabana batewe n’iyo nkongi. Nyuma hagiye hatangazwa ko agaciro k’ibicuruzwa byangiritse kari hejuru ya miliyari 24 Frw.

Nyuma yaho izindi nyubako z’ubucuruzi mu Mujyi wa Kigali zirimo akabari ka Sport Light Lounge, Gisozi Trading Centre, n’Agakiriro n’izindi, zagiye zibasirwa n’inkongi y’umuriro. Izi mpanuka n’izindi zigaragaza ko inkongi ishobora gutungurana, ikibasira inyubako zitandukanye, bigatuma gutegura uburyo abantu bose bashobora kuyisohokamo ari kimwe mu bintu bidakwiye gukerenswa igihe zirimo kubakwa.

Yvonne Uwamahoro ufite ubumuga bw’ingingo, avuga ko bagira cyane impungenge ziterwa no kuba inyubako rusange zitagira ahantu hihariye hagenewe abafite ubumuga mu gihe cy’ubutabazi bwihutirwa.

Ati “Niba inkongi ibaye nta hantu h’ubutabazi hagenewe abantu bafite ubumuga, n’ubusanzwe tuba dufite integer nke, abo muri kumwe ako kanya muri iyo nyubako baraguhutaza, bityo ugasanga n’inkongi yagusangamo kuko nta kwitabara ufite. Nk’uko mu itegeko riturengera havuga ko abantu bafite ubumuga bagomba gutabarwa mbere, n’abubaka izo nyubako bakwiye kubiteganya kandi hakaba n’ababishinzwe ku buryo icyo kiza kibaye batabara hakiri kare.”

Umuyobozi Nshingwabikorwa w’Umuryango rusange w’abantu bafite ubumuga bw’ingingo mu Rwanda (AGHR), Faustin Renzaho, avuga ko kubaka inzu zorohereza abafite ubumuga mu gihe cyo kwinjira, byagakwiye kujyana no kujyana kubateganyiriza aho bashobora gusohokera mu gihe cy’ibiza.

Ati “Iyo haje inkongi ducungiye kuri kiriya cyuma kizamura abantu (Lift/ Ascenseur), nicyo cya mbere gihagarara, icyo gihe biba byarangiye. Niyo mpamvu abantu bakagiye bibuka icyo kintu, cyane ko muri iyi minsi turimo kubona inkongi hirya no hino. Hakabaye hari inzira abantu bafite ubumuga banyuramo mu buryo bworoshye.”

Ikibazo cy’inzira zishobora korohereza abantu bafite ubumuga mu nyubako rusange mu gihe cy’ibiza, ngo gikwiye kujyana no gutegura ahantu hihariye habo abantu bahurizwa muri icyo gihe (Assembly Point).

Renzaho ati “Usang aba nyiri nzu bafata ahantu h’umusigara, hagoye kugera, hakaba ari ho bavuga abantu bahurira mu gihe ibiza bije. Aha naho turasaba ko byahinduka hagatunganywa ku buryo naho haba aho umuntu ufite ubumuga yagera mu buryo bumworoheye, kugira ngo tubungabunge uburenganzira bwe ariko n’ubuzima bw’aAbanyarwanda bamwe mu gihe habaye ibiza.”

Iteka rya Minisitiri w'Ibikorwa Remezo No 1 ryo mu 2009 rigena uburyo inyubako zitangirwamo serivisi zitandukanye zigomba kubakwa kugira ngo abafite ubumuga bazigereho bitabagoye.

Ingingo ya gatatu y'iri teka ivuga ko inyubako zose zigomba kugira ibikoresho n'ibikorwa remezo bifasha abafite ubumuga kugera kuri serivisi zitangirwamo. Ibi bireba inyubako za Leta, iz'abikorera, iz'amadini n'izindi zose zitangirwamo serivisi zigenewe abaturage.

Iri teka rinavuga ko n'inyubako zari zisanzweho mbere y'uko ritangazwa mu Igazeti ya Leta zigomba kubahiriza ibyo risaba. Ingingo ya kane isaba ko inyubako zitangirwamo serivisi zigira aho abafite ubumuga bashobora guhagarika ibinyabiziga byabo hafi y'aho binjirira, ku buryo bibafasha kugera kuri serivisi no kubona ubufasha bwihuse igihe bibaye ngombwa.

Hari kandi Igitabo cy'Amabwiriza y'Imyubakire mu Rwanda (Rwanda Building Code 2019), cyasohotse mu Igazeti ya Leta yo ku wa 16 Mata 2019, gishyiraho ibisabwa birambuye ku buryo inyubako zigomba kubakwa, harimo n'uburyo zitegurwa kugira ngo abantu bazisohokemo mu gihe habaye impanuka.

Iki gitabo gifite igice cyihariye kivuga ku buryo bwo kugera mu nyubako no kuyisohokamo (Accessibility and Evacuation), ndetse n'ibisabwa mu myubakire yita ku bafite ubumuga.

Mu ngingo ya 1.5.12, amabwiriza asaba ko inyubako zose, zirimo iz'ubucuruzi, iz'amashuri, iz'ubuvuzi, iz'amadini, iz'ibiro n'izo guturamo, zitegurwa ku buryo abafite ubumuga bashobora kuzigeramo no gukoresha ibikorwa remezo byazo.

Ikindi gice cy'ingenzi kiri muri Rwanda Building Code 2019 ni icyerekeye uburyo abantu bagomba gusohoka mu nyubako igihe habaye inkongi cyangwa ikindi cyago. Ingingo ya 3.10.2.1 isaba ko buri nyubako igira gahunda yateguwe mbere y'uko impanuka iba, igaragaza uko abantu bazasohoka, uko bazamenyeshwa ibyago, n'uko hazagenzurwa ko abayirimo bose babashije kuyisohokamo.

Iyi gahunda igomba kandi kwita ku bantu bafite ubumuga, abarwaye cyangwa abakomeretse bashobora kugira imbogamizi zo gusohoka bonyine. By'umwihariko, amabwiriza ateganya ko hagomba kugaragazwa inzira iboneye yo gusohora abantu bafite ubumuga, ndetse n'uko abafite ubumuga bwo kutabona bazitabwaho mu myitozo isanzwe yo gusohoka mu nyubako igihe habaye ikibazo.

Ibi bivuze ko inyubako idakwiye kugira ibyapa byerekana aho abantu basohokera gusa, ahubwo igomba no kuba ifite gahunda isobanutse y'uko buri wese, harimo n'udashobora kugenda cyangwa kubona neza, azarokorwa.

Amabwiriza anasaba ko imiryango isohokerwamo mu gihe cy'impanuka ishobora gufungurwa bitagombye urufunguzo cyangwa ubundi bumenyi bwihariye, kandi ko inzira zo gusohoka zigira amatara yihariye akomeza gukora nubwo umuriro w'amashanyarazi waba wacitse.

Ku rundi ruhande ariko nubwo hari amategeko n’amabwiriza bisobanutse, ibisubizo ku bibazo byagaragajwe muri iyi nkuru biracyari kure kuko bitabwaho nkuko bikwiye.

Bigaragarira mu Igenzura ryakozwe na AGHR, ku bufatanye n’inzego zirimo Ikigo cy’Igihugu gishinzwe guteza imbere Imiturire (RHA) n’Urugaga rw’Abenjeniyeri mu Rwanda, rigakorerwa ku nyubako 30 zirimo amashuri, amavuriro, ibiro by’inzego za Leta, amabanki, ibigo by’imari, ahakorerwa imyidagaduro, gare n’insengero, ryagaragaje ko 38% ari zo zujuje ibisabwa kugira ngo abafite ubumuga bw’ingingo bazigeremo banaziboneremo serivisi.

Naho uburyo bwihariye bwo gutabara no korohereza abafite ubumuga mu gihe cy’ibiza nk’inkongi y’umuriro ntabwo byitaweho cyane muri iryo genzura kuko ababyubahirije ari mbarwa.

“Sinigeze ntekereza ko nzaba muri Afurika. Nari mfite gahunda yo kujya muri Espagne cyangwa muri Portugal, ariko inshuti yanjye iranyumvisha ngo mbanze nsure Afurika.”

Iyi ni yo ntangiriro y’urugendo rwa Ole Havgum, Umunyanoruveje ubu umaze hafi imyaka umunani aba mu Rwanda, aho yashinze ibikorwa bya Fitness Point bimaze kugira amashami ane y’imyitozo ngororamubiri mu Mujyi wa Kigali.

Havgum avuga ko mbere atigeze atekereza ko Afurika ari ho yazubakira ubuzima n’ubucuruzi. Nyuma yo kugirwa inama n’inshuti yo gusura uyu mugabane, yaje mu Rwanda mu 2018 agamije kureba uko ibikorwa by’imyitozo ngororamubiri bihagaze mu Mujyi wa Kigali.

Ibyo yabonye byamuhaye igitekerezo cyo kuhakorera. Yasanze urwego rw’ibigo by’imyitozo ngororamubiri mu Rwanda rutaragera aho yari yarubonye mu bihugu yakoreyemo, maze abona amahirwe yo kuzana ubundi buryo bwo gukora siporo. Mu 2019, yafashe icyemezo cyo kwimukira mu Rwanda no gutangiza ibikorwa bye.

Havgum yari asanzwe afite ubunararibonye muri uru rwego kuva mu 1989, aho yari yarakoreye ibikorwa by’imyitozo ngororamubiri muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika no muri Noruveje. Yabaye umukinnyi wabigize umwuga, yatoza abakinnyi begukanye ibikombe by’isi, kandi afite impamyabumenyi y’icyiciro cya gatatu cya kaminuza mu bijyanye na siporo.

Uyu munsi, Fitness Point ifite amashami ane manini i Kigali, ikoresha abakozi bari hagati ya 80 na 100. Ibikorwa byayo byagutse birimo ibyumba by’imyitozo bifite ibikoresho bitandukanye, pisine zo kogeramo, sauna, ikibuga cya basketball, amasomo ya spinning na aerobics.

Ifite kandi amashami yihariye y’abagore i Remera no muri Kanombe. Havgum avuga ko uko ibikorwa byagutse ari na ko abantu benshi batangiye kubona amahirwe yo gukora siporo hafi y’aho batuye cyangwa bakorera, ndetse n’ibigo by’ubucuruzi bikaba biri kwiyongera mu bakiriya bayo.

Avuga ko isoko ry’imyitozo ngororamubiri mu Rwanda ryamwibukije uko ryari rimeze mu Burayi no muri Amerika mu myaka 20 cyangwa 30 ishize. Yizera ko hari amahirwe menshi yo gukomeza kuriteza imbere, kandi ko afite gahunda yo kwagura ibikorwa.

Ku bwe, siporo ntigomba gufatwa nk’igikorwa kigenewe abashaka kugira imikaya cyangwa umubiri ugaragara neza gusa. Ni ingenzi ku bantu b’ingeri zose, harimo n’abafite imyaka iri hagati ya 50 na 70, kuko intego nyamukuru ari ukugira ubuzima bwiza.

Havgum asaba abifuza gutangira ubucuruzi gukorera ku kintu bakunda kandi bafitiye ishyaka, ariko bakirinda kwihutira kwagura ibikorwa batarubaka umusingi ukomeye.

Ati: “Niba hari ikintu ukunda kandi ugifitiye ishyaka, tangirira kuri bike, hanyuma ugende wagura ibikorwa byawe.”
